### Investment Memo: COHR — November 9, 2026

**Verdict**: BUY | Conviction: **Medium**
**Price Target**: $285 (~48% upside from current $192.81)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

⚠️ *Process note: the Value Researcher produced no report. Valuation inputs below are cross-drawn from the Growth, Quant and Short agents plus directly pulled multiples (46.8x trailing P/E, 25.2x EV/EBITDA, 19.7x FY27E, negative P/FCF). No independent intrinsic-value estimate exists in this pack — treat the sell-side mean target (~$390–405) as a ceiling reference, not an anchor. All other domains reviewed, including macro and risk.*

---

**Investment Thesis**

Coherent is the only vertically integrated InP/optics supplier at scale in a capacity-constrained AI datacom market growing >40% CAGR, with revenue re-accelerating (+49.9% YoY in Q1 FY27, >60% FY27 pro forma guide), gross margin up 820bps in two years, a $20B contracted backlog anchor, and a balance sheet that cannot be forced to refinance before 2029. The 56% drawdown from the June peak was manufactured by macro (10Y at 5.13%, hyperscaler capex trims) and sector beta, not by any deterioration in company data — 7/7 beats, flat receivables days, expanding margins. The offsetting reality: this is a 95%-volatility, 3.4-beta instrument that converts only ~10% of earnings to cash, has 212 days of inventory, and has diluted holders ~30% in five quarters — so the position must be sized and gated, not chased.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector is early-to-mid volume cycle (ATTRACTIVE): InP fab capacity is the binding constraint, pricing power is positive, and the Marvell–Lumentum deal (~$115B) removes COHR's closest independent rival for 18+ months. Macro is UNFAVOURABLE on the *multiple*, not the business — bear steepener (10Y 5.13%, 30Y 5.47%), core PCE stuck at 3.12%, hikes being priced, and hyperscaler capex guidance trims. Macro bear case: $130–150. Wildcard: FCC ban on Chinese transceivers (~51% share) would be a large share-shift windfall.
- **Geopolitical & Legal (MEDIUM)**: Direct China revenue <10%, but the majority of employees and key III-V fabs are in Asia — operational exposure exceeds revenue exposure. Top risk: Chinese export-control retaliation on gallium/germanium/InP feedstock (40–50% probability of material disruption in 12–18 months). Securities class action (2020–25 class period) is disclosure-noise, not existential. No DOJ/SEC/BIS enforcement history.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: ⚠️ *Dedicated report missing.* Composite picture: optically expensive trailing (46.8x P/E, 25.2x EV/EBITDA, negative FCF) but inexpensive on forward earnings (19.7x FY27E, 12.8x FY28E EPS of $15.01; PEG ~0.25). P/B 3.35x vs LITE 8.65x. The value case is entirely a forward-earnings case — it fails if estimates fail.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth (STRONG BUY)**: FY26 $7.12B (+22.5%) → Q1 FY27 +49.9%; Datacenter & Comms now ~80%+ of sales at +79% YoY. GM 30.9%→39.1% across seven quarters; order book visible to 2028; 1.6T ramp and CPO content provide next-leg optionality. FY27E EPS $9.81 → FY29E $21.24. Caveat: FY29–30 estimates rest on 1–4 analysts.
- **Quantitative Signals (NEUTRAL / Sell-bias)**: Sharpe 0.24, Sortino 0.37, alpha −5.5%, vol 95.6%, max DD −60.2%. 12-1 momentum +25.5% masks a −43% skip month — a textbook momentum-crash setup at 22% of the 52-week range. Risk is statistically uncompensated *to date*; the earnings-revision "signal" is a single-analyst artifact.
- **Financial Risk (MODERATE — split)**: Credit/liquidity LOW: net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x, interest coverage 8.2x, $2.0B cash, $4B facility, no maturities before 2029, BB positive outlook. Cash conversion HIGH risk: FY26 OCF $80M vs NI $805M; inventory +105% to $3.3B (212 days); Q1 FY27 FCF ≈ −$868M. Equity market risk HIGH (beta 2.77–3.46). Solvency is remote even in a −20% revenue scenario.
- **Non-Financial Risk (HIGH)**: Three stacked items — the class action, the China InP licence chokepoint feeding the entire growth thesis, and extreme customer concentration (two >10% customers plus one $20B contract). Governance structure is a genuine offset (independent chair, no duality, TSR-linked PSUs), but insider activity is one-sided: Chair, CFO and CTO sold ~$9.9M at $268–426 with zero open-market buys into the drawdown. Escalate: confirm 10b5-1 adoption dates.
- **ESG (NEUTRAL)**: Not a thesis driver. 78% renewable electricity, no material controversy (~$203k lifetime penalties). The financeable ESG risks are operational (fab safety cadence, Asian supply-chain labour audits gating shipments) and governance (verify whether PSUs reward *building* capacity vs *earning a return on* it — proxy CD&A unverified).
- **Alternative Data (BULLISH, medium confidence)**: 100% beat rate with stable +6.6% avg surprise; hiring mix confirms capacity ramp; news sentiment flipped positive post-midterms; S&P 500 inclusion; COHR outperforming LITE 2.4x on the bounce. Google Trends collapse is narrative decay, not demand. Feb 3 print tracking modestly above consensus.
- **Short / Contrarian View (NO EDGE — short rejected)**: Earnings quality is genuinely low (FCF conversion −128%, accruals swing positive, promotional "pro forma" guidance post-divestiture, 730bps GAAP/non-GAAP gap) — but every dollar of the cash gap is traceable to *disclosed* inventory build and capex. GMI 0.944 and flat DSO actively disconfirm manipulation. The short has already paid (−49%); shorting a 50%-grower at ~13x FY28E on accounting grounds is unjustifiable. The deciding variable: whether Q2 FY27 operating cash flow turns positive.

**Where agents disagree — and how it resolves**: Growth (Strong Buy) vs Quant (Sell bias) vs Macro (Unfavourable) are answering different questions: the earnings path vs the return distribution vs the discount rate. Resolution: the multiple headwind dominates over ~3 months; the earnings case dominates over 24 months. Hence scaled entry with a hard cash-flow gate, not a full position and not a pass.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Structural scarcity + consolidation**: only vertically integrated InP supplier at scale; Lumentum absorbed by Marvell; possible FCC ban on Chinese transceivers (~51% share) — three simultaneous share/pricing tailwinds.
- **Estimate momentum through a de-rated multiple**: >60% FY27 pro forma guide, $3B quarter by Jun-27, 7/7 beats, GM marching toward 45% — 12.8x FY28E EPS with an order book to 2028.
- **Balance sheet survives the bear case**: ~1.0x net leverage, $2B cash, no maturities before 2029, full discretionary control over the $3B capex program (~4.5 years of runway even at current burn).

**Bear Case**
- **Cash conversion failure**: $805M net income produced $80M of operating cash; 212 inventory days in a fast-obsolescence market; a 20% write-down ≈ two quarters of GAAP operating income.
- **Discount-rate + capex double-hit**: 100bp higher required return = −18–30% on the multiple alone; one more hyperscaler capex trim re-rates the stock violently (it fell ~50% in five weeks on a $5B Microsoft trim).
- **Dilution and concentration**: ~30% share count growth in five quarters, insiders selling into strength with zero buys, and FY27–28 visibility resting on a handful of hyperscalers plus one $20B contract and a politicised InP supply line.

**Key Risks**
1. Q2 FY27 (Feb 3, 2027) operating cash flow stays negative with inventory >$4B → thesis downgrades to Short-candidate (the Short analyst's own trigger).
2. China export-licence interruption of InP/gallium/germanium feedstock, or BIS action touching a COHR customer.
3. Hyperscaler capex digestion / AI-spend policy shock (post-midterm Congress, state data-center resistance).
4. Further equity issuance at current prices; PhotonLink termination/repricing/volume-flex.
5. CPO architecture displacement of pluggables accelerating beyond COHR's content capture (2028+ risk).

**Portfolio Construction Note** (from Portfolio Strategist)

**Initiate 1.5%, hard cap 3.0%, in three tranches**: 0.75% at market (~$190–196); 0.75% only on a $165–178 retest that holds *or* a confirmed close above $215–220 on >12M shares; final 0.75–1.0% **gated on positive Q2 FY27 operating cash flow on Feb 3, 2027** — do not exceed 1.5% before then. Correlations: LITE 0.83, FN 0.79, CIEN 0.76 — COHR is a *substitute*, never a complement, for existing optical holdings; fund from those if present. Pass entirely if the book is already long AI-momentum/high-beta hardware. Hard stop: weekly close below $148. Trims: −25% at $330, −40% at $390–405; enforce 3.0% cap mechanically. Thesis invalidation: two sequential GM declines, FY27 guide cut below 40%, InP licence event (halve immediately), or any new dilutive raise. This is a satellite growth position sized for a 60%-drawdown instrument — sizing is the risk control, the stop is the backstop.

**The one number to calendar: February 3, 2027 — operating cash flow.** Everything in this thesis is downstream of whether ~$385M of quarterly GAAP profit starts converting to cash.

# COHR — Portfolio Construction Recommendation
**Coherent Corp. | NYSE: COHR | Price $192.81 | Mkt cap $37.67B | EV $39.22B | Next print: 3 Feb 2027**

## Synthesis Judgment (up front)

The 11 reports do **not** disagree about the business. They disagree about the **equity as an instrument**. Every agent with a fundamentals mandate — Sector, Growth, Alt Data, even the Short analyst in his own bear-case rebuttal — confirms accelerating revenue (+49.9% YoY), expanding gross margin (30.9%→39.1% over seven quarters), a 100% beat rate, and a physical moat in InP capacity. No agent alleges fraud. The Short analyst's manipulation hypothesis *fails on the evidence* (GMI 0.944, DSO flat).

What the risk agents are actually saying is different and more serious: **the multiple is the asset, and the multiple is under attack from outside the company** (Macro: 10Y 5.13%, core PCE 3.12%, hyperscaler capex trims) **and from inside the cash flow statement** (Fin Risk / Short: OCF $80M against $805M net income; inventory days 140→212; ~30% dilution). Neither of those is a reason to avoid the name. Both are reasons to **size it like a 95%-volatility instrument rather than a 20%-growth compounder** — which is what the growth camp's "$400 target" framing implicitly does not do.

Net weighted conviction: **positive but second-tier.** This is a *satellite growth position*, not a core holding.

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Attractive sector; COHR "Strong" | **High** | Capacity-constrained, not demand-constrained. Only vertically integrated player at scale. But **highest beta in group (2.23)** and heaviest capital needs. |
| **Growth Researcher** | **STRONG BUY** | **High** | >60% FY27 guide; 19.7x FY27E / 12.8x FY28E EPS; PEG ~0.25; order book to 2028. Sizes as growth *satellite*, not core. |
| **Alt Data Analyst** | **BULLISH** | **Medium** (feed failures) | 7/7 beats, +6.6% avg surprise, S&P 500 inclusion, Lumentum distracted by Marvell deal. −61% drawdown is *sector beta*, not company data. |
| **Fin Risk Analyst** | **MODERATE** (split) | **Medium-High** | Credit risk **LOW** (0.99x net debt/EBITDA, no maturities before 2029, BB positive). Market risk **HIGH**. **Cash conversion risk HIGH.** |
| **Short Analyst** | **NO EDGE — reject short** | **High** | "Low-quality earnings, but not fabricated." Cash gap fully explained by disclosed inventory ($1,143M) + capex. Short has already paid (−49% from peak). **Do not own either.** |
| **Nonfin Risk Analyst** | **HIGH** | **Medium** | Securities class action + China InP chokepoint + two >10% customers + a $20B single-customer contract. Offset: independent chair, no duality, no SEC actions. |
| **Geo / Legal** | **MEDIUM** | **Medium** | China revenue <10% but **majority of employees and key fabs in Asia**. Gallium/germanium/rare-earth retaliation = 40–50% probability of material disruption in 12–18 months. |
| **Macro Researcher** | **UNFAVOURABLE** | **High** | Bear steepener (10Y 5.13%, 30Y 5.47%), Fed pricing hikes, capex guidance trims. Bear case **$130–150**. Explicitly *not* a sell on the business. |
| **Quant Analyst** | **NEUTRAL / Sell bias** | **Medium** | Sharpe 0.24, Sortino 0.37, alpha **−5.5%**, beta **3.46**, max DD 60.2%. 12-1 momentum +25.5% masks a −43% skip month. Classic momentum-crash setup. |
| **ESG Analyst** | **NEUTRAL / Average** | Low relevance | Not a thesis driver. Watch item: whether PSUs reward *building* capacity or *earning a return on* it — unverified, proxy blocked. |
| **Value Researcher** | **⚠ NO REPORT PRODUCED** | — | **Gap.** I substitute directly-pulled ratios (below). No independent intrinsic-value estimate exists in this pack. |

**Direct valuation verification (my own pull, substituting for the missing Value agent):** P/E 46.8x trailing · EV/EBITDA 25.2x trailing · **P/FCF −36.6x** · P/B 3.35x · no dividend. Analyst targets $350–450 (mean ≈$405) — but note **Rosenblatt cut to $400 and Susquehanna cut $425→$350 in the same fortnight**. The sell-side is trailing the multiple compression, not leading it. I treat $405 as a *ceiling reference*, not a price anchor.

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **MEDIUM**

**High agreement (5 agents) — the operating business:**
Sector, Growth, Alt Data, Fin Risk and Short all independently confirm the same operating facts: revenue re-accelerating, gross margin expanding for four consecutive quarters, InP capacity as the binding industry constraint, and a legitimately de-risked balance sheet (0.99x net leverage, no maturities until 2029). This is about as clean a fundamental consensus as this framework produces.

**Genuine split (4 agents) — the equity:**
Growth says 19.7x FY27E is "too cheap." Quant says Sharpe 0.24 with negative alpha is "not compensated." These are not contradictory — they are answering different questions. Growth is pricing the *earnings path*; Quant is pricing the *distribution of returns*. At 95.6% annualized volatility, both can be right simultaneously.

**Conflict resolved — Macro vs Growth:**
The decisive tension is Macro's discount-rate case (−18% to −30% fair value from a 100bp required-return shift) against Growth's earnings case (+51% revenue, +75% EPS). **Neither overrides the other; they compound.** The resolution is that the earnings case wins over 24 months and the discount-rate case wins over 3 months. That mandates scale-in entry and a cash-flow gate, not a pass and not a full position.

**Conflict resolved — Nonfin/Geo risk precedence:**
Per framework rule, a live risk flag outranks a bullish fundamental view when it can permanently impair capital. Here it can't: the InP chokepoint and class action are **timing risks against a fully-booked order book**, not solvency or fraud risks. So they *reduce* size, they do not veto.

**The one that should genuinely worry the committee:** nobody in the pack can tell you whether Q2 FY27 operating cash flow turns positive. That single line item is the fulcrum between "cheap cyclical" and "EPS air-pocket," and it is 85 days away.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.5% initiate → 3.0% maximum**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Initial position** | **1.5% of portfolio** (75% of it at market; 25% held for the Feb 3 gate) |
| **Maximum position** | **3.0%** — hard cap, no exceptions |
| **Framework bucket** | *Medium-to-elevated risk, medium-high conviction* → normally 1–3%; capped at the top of that band rather than the 3–5% high-conviction band |
| **Kelly check** | Full Kelly on my scenario weights (55% up +55%, 45% down −30%) implies **~30%** of capital. Half-Kelly = 15%. **I am running at one-fifth of half-Kelly.** |

**Why the Kelly number is discarded, deliberately.** Kelly assumes a known distribution; COHR's distribution is fat-tailed and regime-dependent. A 15% position in a 95.6%-vol, 3.46-beta stock contributes ~14% portfolio volatility on its own and would dominate every other risk decision in the book. The binding constraint is not edge — it is that **a demonstrated 60% peak-to-trough drawdown at 3% position size costs 1.8% of portfolio, which is survivable; at 15% it costs 9%, which is a career event.**

**Why not smaller (0.5–1%)?** Because the edge is real and cross-confirmed: 7/7 beats, expanding margins, a competitor removed for 18+ months by the Marvell–Lumentum deal, and a stock at 22% of its 52-week range on *improving* fundamentals. Under-sizing a verified dislocation is its own error.

**Sizing is the primary risk control here. The stop-loss is secondary.**

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector / correlation — the most important finding of this review:**

| Pair | 252-day correlation | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| COHR–**LITE** | **0.83** | Near-substitutes. **Never hold both.** |
| COHR–**FN** | **0.79** | Do not hold alongside. |
| COHR–**CIEN** | 0.76 | Adds little diversification. |
| COHR–**MTSI** | 0.75 | Overlapping optics exposure. |
| COHR–**ANET** | 0.55 | Acceptable pairing. |
| COHR–**NVDA** | **0.54** | **Genuinely useful.** COHR is *not* merely an NVDA proxy. |

**The actionable conclusion:** COHR is a **consolidation candidate, not an addition**, if the book already holds Lumentum, Fabrinet, Ciena or MACOM. Fund the new 1.5% by exiting or halving an existing optical holding — the 0.83 LITE correlation means the marginal diversification benefit of holding both is near zero while the idiosyncratic risk (InP licence denial, a single $20B contract) is entirely additive. Against NVDA or ANET at 0.54–0.55, COHR adds real diversification *within* the same AI-capex theme.

**Factor exposure — this is a deliberate, offsetting trade, and must be approved as such:**

| Factor | COHR tilt | Book impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Momentum** | **Strongly positive** (12-1 +25.5%) | ⚠️ **Crowded.** The AI-optics momentum theme is where the last 18 months of returns came from. Adding here is adding to the crowded leg. |
| **Value** | Strongly negative (46.8x P/E, negative FCF) | Deepens growth-bias. |
| **Quality** | Negative (ROE 7.2%, accruals +3.96%, F-Score 6/9) | Lowers book quality score. |
| **Low Volatility** | **Severely negative** (95.6% vol, β 3.46) | ⚠️ **The dominant effect.** This single position will be the largest contributor to portfolio VaR. |
| **Size** | Mid-cap $38B | Neutral. |

**Net:** this position trades *down* quality, value and stability to buy *up* momentum and growth. It is only appropriate for a portfolio that is **already quality-and-value-tilted and currently underweight high-beta growth** — or for a book where COHR is being funded out of another AI-momentum name. For a portfolio already long AI/momentum/high-beta, the correct action is **Pass**, not Initiate.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in across three tranches — do not buy the full position at once**

Current price $192.81 sits **48% below the lowest analyst target** and **22% up its 52-week range** ($123.75–$440.00). The stock made a capitulation low of **$160.23 on 5 November on 17.3M shares** and snapped back **+13.6% to $192.81 the next session on 16.3M shares**. Two heavy-volume reversal days is a *bounce*, not a *base* — and with a 6.0% daily sigma, chasing a +13.6% single-session move is paying up for noise.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **0.75%** | Now, at market ≈$190–196 | Establishes exposure to the dislocation. The fundamental case does not require a better price. |
| **2** | **0.75%** | *(a)* retest of **$165–178 that holds**, **OR** *(b)* convincing close above **$215–220** on >12M shares | Buy either the retest or the confirmation, never the middle. Avoids both value-traps and momentum chases. |
| **3** | **0.75–1.0%** | **ONLY after the 3 Feb 2027 print**, and **only if** Q2 FY27 operating cash flow turns positive **OR** inventory days compress toward 150 | This is the Short analyst's single deciding variable — the fulcrum between "cheap cyclical" and "EPS air-pocket." Do not pre-pay for it. |

**Do not exceed 1.5% before February 3.** The information value of the Q2 cash flow line exceeds the expected return of two extra months of exposure.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**A. Hard price stop: weekly close below $148 (−23% from entry).**
Deliberately set below the $160.23 capitulation low and at the top of Macro's $130–150 bear-case band. **Use a weekly close, not intraday** — at 6.0% daily sigma, an intraday stop in this name is a donation to the market. *Note the honest limitation:* a 23% stop is only ~3.8 daily sigmas and can be hit on no news. This is why sizing (3% cap ⇒ a full 50% drawdown costs 1.5% of portfolio) is the actual risk control and the stop is a backstop.

**B. Thesis invalidation — exit on any one of these, regardless of price:**
1. **Cash flow** — Q2 FY27 (3 Feb 2027) operating cash flow still negative **and** inventory above $4.0B **and** revenue growth decelerating below 40%. → **Exit fully.** This is the Short analyst's own upgrade-to-Short trigger.
2. **Gross margin** declines sequentially for two consecutive quarters. Breaks the pricing-power thesis that Sector, Growth and Short all rest on.
3. **FY27 pro forma growth guide cut below 40%** (from >60% today).
4. **InP supply** — any BIS licence denial, or a Chinese export-licence interruption touching InP/gallium/germanium feedstock. → **Halve immediately** (Geo's escalation trigger to HIGH).
5. **Another dilutive equity raise** at current prices. The ~30% dilution across five quarters is already the strongest governance criticism in the pack; a further raise at $193 would confirm the equity is funding the capex program.
6. **Customer concentration event** — a PhotonLink termination, repricing, or volume-flex invocation.

**C. Trim triggers:**
- **First trim (−25% of position) at $330** — ~22x FY28E EPS of $15.01, and ~82% of mean analyst target.
- **Second trim (−40% of remaining) at $390–405** — mean target; **≈90–100% of the only intrinsic-value reference available.** With the Value Researcher's report missing, I am unwilling to hold through the sell-side's own ceiling.
- **Final residual** held into FY2028 to test the "$4B quarter" commitment.
- **Position cap enforcement:** if appreciation carries COHR above **3.5%** of portfolio, trim mechanically back to 3.0%.

**D. Portfolio-level monitor:** if any of LITE / FN / CIEN / MTSI is added later, **reduce COHR pro rata** — the 0.75–0.83 correlations make those positions substitutes, not complements.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — small, scaled, cash-flow-gated**

> **Initiate at 1.5% of portfolio** (0.75% at market; 0.75% on a $165–178 retest hold or a confirmed break above $215–220), **with a third tranche of 0.75–1.0% explicitly gated on Q2 FY27 operating cash flow turning positive on 3 February 2027. Hard maximum 3.0%.**

**Conditions on the action:**
- **Initiate** if the book is underweight high-beta growth, or if the position is funded by exiting LITE/FN/CIEN (correlations 0.76–0.83).
- **Pass** if the portfolio is already long AI-momentum or high-beta hardware, or if aggregate optical/AI-datacenter exposure would exceed a prudent single-theme limit. In that case COHR is a *substitute* for an existing holding, not an addition.
- **Do not short** — the Short analyst's forensic case is correctly rejected. The cash gap is disclosed inventory and disclosed capex, receivables days are flat, and the short has already paid −49%.

**What would move this to Add (4–5%):** Q2 FY27 operating cash flow positive + inventory days compressing + gross margin ≥40% + the >60% FY27 guide reiterated. All four, not three.

**What would move this to Exit:** any single Clause 6(B) invalidation trigger.

**The one number the committee should put in the calendar:** **3 February 2027, operating cash flow.** Everything else in this thesis — the multiple, the target price, the sizing — is downstream of whether ~$385M of quarterly GAAP profit starts converting into cash.

Coherent sits in the optical components and photonics layer of the AI data-centre supply chain — InP/GaAs lasers, optical transceivers, high-precision optics and semiconductor capital equipment. 4. **Architecture risk (CPO vs. pluggables).** If co-packaged optics displaces pluggable transceivers faster than Coherent monetizes CPO content, its largest revenue pool compresses. Partially hedged, not fully.

## 2. Key Red Flags Found

1. **Working capital is eating all the profit.** FY2026 change in working capital **−$1,102M** on revenue of $7,118M. Inventory alone absorbed ~$1,143M. Q1 FY27 added another **−$644M** — the drag is *widening*, not normalising.

3. **Capex 5.3x depreciation.** Q1 FY27 capex $775M vs D&A $147M; annualising ~$3.1B of capex against ~$590M of D&A. The depreciation cliff is *ahead*, not behind — a mechanical gross-margin headwind arriving FY27–FY28 regardless of demand.
4. **~30% dilution in five quarters.** Diluted weighted shares 155.5M (Q4 FY25) → 195.4M (FY26) → **202.0M (Q1 FY27)**. Equity rose $3.18B from Jun-25 to Sep-26 against cumulative net income of ~$1.19B, implying ~$1.8–1.9B of net share issuance. Basic 196.2M vs diluted 202.0M signals a convertible overhang. Piotroski F7 (no dilution) = 0. **Per-share value creation is materially worse than headline growth.**
5. **Guidance re-engineered on "pro forma" basis.** On 14 Oct 2026 the company agreed to sell its Materials Processing Tools division to Bystronic, then guided FY27 to ">60% pro forma revenue growth." Divesting a business mechanically raises the growth rate on a smaller denominator. "First $3B quarter by FY-end, first $4B quarter in FY2028, >45% non-GAAP GM before end-CY2028" is a promotional stack of ever-dated promises.
6. **Non-GAAP gap of ~730bps.** Q1 FY27 GAAP operating margin 15.9% vs non-GAAP 23.2% — ~$173M/quarter (~$690M/yr) of add-backs, ~30% of GAAP operating income. Note GAAP operating margin **fell** YoY (16.4% → 15.9%) even as non-GAAP rose 368bps.
7. **Intangibles stretched.** Goodwill + intangibles $7,264M = 36% of assets, 62% of equity. The FY2026 10-K discloses a *quantitative* impairment test of the "Coherent" trade name — management itself flagged the carrying value as close to the line.
8. **Insider selling, no buying.** 14 open-market sales totalling ~$9.95M over six months, clustered in the days immediately after the 7 Aug 2026 peak ($379). A director sold 2,200 shares at $268 on 2 Sep 2026 **outside a 10b5-1 plan**. Dollar size is modest for a $38B cap — a yellow flag, not red.

**Where the red flags are notably *absent*:** receivables. Annual AR grew 31.7% vs revenue 22.5% (flag triggered), but this has fully normalised — at Q1 FY27 receivables grew **49.6% vs revenue 49.9%**, with DSO flat at ~62 days year-over-year. ## 3. Beneish M-Score & Accruals Analysis

- **M-Score: −1.803** — inside the "possible manipulator" band (−2.22 to −1.78), barely.
- **But the score is not usable as evidence.** DEPI of 9.515 implies the depreciation rate collapsed ~90% (actual: D&A/revenue ≈ 7.3% vs 9.5% prior year) and AQI of −0.887 is off an impossible PP&E figure. Strip out the two corrupted indices and the *reliable* components are benign: **GMI 0.944** (gross margin index below 1.0 = margins improving — anti-manipulation), **DSRI 1.075** (receivables days +7.5%, modest, and now reversed), **LVGI 0.895** (leverage falling), **SGI 1.225**, **TATA 0.0396**.
- **Accruals ratio: +0.0396** — positive and a ~+0.079 swing from FY25's −0.039, but still *below* the 0.05 warning threshold. On a balance-sheet basis this is high-normal for a company ramping capacity 50%+, not manipulation.
- **Piotroski F-Score: 6/9** (moderate). Failures: accruals quality, no dilution, asset turnover.

**Verdict: earnings are low-quality, but they are not fabricated.** The cash gap is *fully explained by disclosed line items* — inventory and capex — not by revenue recognition, capitalised opex, or related-party fiction. A Chanos-style "the cash isn't there" short requires the cash to be *missing*; here it is *visibly spent*.

## 6. Short Thesis Summary — Is there a credible bear case?

**A credible *quality* bear case, yes. A credible *fraud* case, no.**

**The bear case that holds:**
> COHR is an AI-optics capex supercycle play consuming ~$870M of cash per quarter at peak narrative. It funds a $3B/yr capex program with negative FCF and ~30% dilution, and its 211 days of inventory is 50% above its own historical norm. The depreciation cliff from that capex arrives in FY27–FY28 and compresses margins mechanically. GAAP operating margin already fell YoY in the best growth quarter in company history. At 3.8x FY27E EV/sales with negative free cash flow, any hyperscaler order digestion produces violent de-rating — the stock fell 20% on 14 Aug 2025 and ~19% on 27 Jan 2025 for exactly this reason.

**The bull case is stronger on the fundamentals, and I must say so:**
Revenue accelerated to +49.9% YoY (from 17.3% three quarters earlier) with gross margin up 254bps — that is the *opposite* of a decelerating, channel-stuffed story. Datacenter & Comms +79%. Management guided Q2 to $2.55–2.75B (a further +8–16% sequentially) and FY27 pro forma growth >60%. Receivables days are flat, so the revenue is being collected. The Altman Z-Score of 1.902 looks alarming only because the tool uses *book* equity; recomputed with market capitalisation (X4 = 4.42) the Z-Score is **~3.8 — the safe zone**. Net debt is $2.79B, leverage is falling (LVGI 0.895), and the industrial divestiture removes a low-margin drag.

**And critically — the short has already paid.** Price is $192.81 vs a 7 Aug 2026 peak of $379.13: **−49%**. It fell 12% on the Q1 FY27 print alone. At ~19.7x FY27E EPS of $9.81 and ~12.8x FY28E EPS of $15.01, this is no longer a crowded-multiple short. Adding fresh short exposure here means betting against a 50–80% grower with expanding margins at a mid-teens forward multiple, to capture a *further* leg of a de-rating that is already two-thirds done.

## 7. Contrarian Rating: **NO EDGE** — Reject the Short Thesis

I cannot certify this as a forensic short. Cash conversion of 10% is genuinely poor and the dilution is shareholder-hostile, but every dollar of the cash gap is traceable to disclosed inventory build and disclosed capex — the signature of a capacity ramp mis-timed against an order book, not of accounting fraud. There is no receivables divergence, no margin collapse, no auditor or related-party event, no restatement, and no solvency issue.

**Positioning:**
- **Do not short for accounting reasons.** The manipulation hypothesis fails on the evidence. GMI of 0.944 and flat DSO are explicit disconfirmations.
- **Do not own it either.** Accruals quality, 211 inventory days, a 5x capex/depreciation ratio and ~30% dilution mean reported EPS materially overstates per-share economics. If the AI datacom order book pauses for even two quarters, the inventory write-down plus depreciation ramp produces an EPS air-pocket that consensus FY28E of $15.01 does not contemplate.
- **The only honest trade is tactical and cyclical, not forensic:** a valuation/beta short on hyperscaler capex digestion, sized small, and only on a rally back toward $260–300. That is a macro bet, not the forensic bet I was asked to underwrite.

**Single most valuable thing to monitor next:** whether Q2 FY27 operating cash flow turns positive as the working-capital build annualises. If inventory passes $4B while revenue growth decelerates below 40%, the bear case upgrades from "quality concern" to **Short**. If OCF flips positive and inventory days compress toward 150, the bull case is vindicated and the stock is cheap. That one line item decides it.
